chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan, from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar, who said:

I asked Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him) about a man who brings me silver (dirhams), so I buy it from him with dinars (gold coins). I occupy myself with checking its weight, evaluating it, and the excess between me and him in it, so I give him the dinars and say to him: 'It is not a sale between me and you, for I have cancelled the sale between us. Your silver with me is a loan, and my dinars with you are a loan, until you come to me tomorrow and I will sell it to you.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem with it.'

key_terms.أَبَا إِبْرَاهِيمَ: Abu Ibrahim (Imam Musa al-Kazim, peace be upon him)

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to delay the finalization of a gold-for-silver trade by converting it into a loan arrangement?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi elucidates the permissibility of 'Bay' al-Ta'liq' (conditional or deferred sale) in Shia jurisprudence, where the buyer converts the immediate exchange of gold and silver into a mutual loan (qard) to avoid the strict requirement of immediate possession (qabd) and weighing. Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) validates this mechanism, highlighting the scholarly distinction between a sale and a loan in commercial contexts to facilitate trade while adhering to the principles of riba-free exchange. This ruling underscores the practical flexibility within Shia fiqh regarding the timing of possession in currency transactions.
